newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates under upward pressure.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates under upward pressure.

text.p: Dutch money rates stabilised at a slightly higher level on Thursday while dealers and investors digested Wednesday's remarks from Bundesbank official Otmar Issing, which quashed rate cut hopes.
"Taking his remarks to the letter, the first thing we can expect is a rise in interest rates," said one dealer, adding there was still far to go before this would happen.
On Wednesday Issing said key rates were at a historic low and there was no reason to expect key rate cuts.
Earlier today, the Bundesbank left the discount and Lombard rates unchanged, which had broadly been expected by the market.
Dealers said guilder deposits might rise a little more as the market was very wary after Issing's remarks.
"After the first shock, rates are likely to stabilise at slightly lower levels," said another dealer.
Dealers said there were very few investors willing to put out money now as they were waiting for the moment to get a slightly higher return.
"It is difficult to find money right now, trade is very thin," said one.
Three-month deposits were bid at 2.84 percent, up two basis points since yesterday.
Call was still trading as high as 2.81/87 percent bid, but dealers said the new special advances pact this afternoon at 1400 GMT would not bring any changes.
The advances rate has been pegged at 2.50 percent for some time.
The guilder was a bit stronger at 112.1725 per 100 marks from 112.19 on Wednesday.
